<thought>The proton NMR spectra show peaks at 1.20 ppm (doublet, 3H), 2.85 ppm (doublet, 2H), 3.09 ppm (quartet, 1H), 3.81 ppm (singlet, 3H), 7.15 ppm (doublet of doublet of doublets, 2H), and 7.92 ppm (doublet of doublet of doublets, 2H). The peaks at 7.15 and 7.92 ppm suggest aromatic protons, while the peak at 3.81 ppm indicates a methoxy group. The peaks at 1.20, 2.85, and 3.09 ppm suggest an ethyl group. Combining this with the carbon NMR data, the compound likely contains an aromatic ring, a methoxy group, and an ethyl group. I will now use the IR spectra to confirm the presence of functional groups, especially the carbonyl group.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>

<thought>The IR spectra show a strong peak at 1739 cm⁻¹, which is indicative of a carbonyl group (C=O). The peaks around 3100-3000 cm⁻¹ suggest aromatic C-H stretching, supporting the presence of an aromatic ring. The data from the NMR and IR spectra suggest the compound could be an aromatic ester, possibly with a methoxy group and an ethyl group. To confirm the structure, I will search for similar structures in the NMRShift database using a potential SMILES string that fits the data: 'COC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1CC'.</thought>
<action>search_by_smiles</action>
<action_input>{"smiles": "COC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1CC", "top_k": 5}</action_input>

<thought>The search results show a close match with the SMILES string 'COC(=O)C1=CC=CC=CC1', which corresponds to methyl benzoate. The carbon NMR data from the database entry (δ: 26.73, 51.99, 121.85, 124.27, 127.11, 129.14, 132.72, 135.34, 166.66) is consistent with the observed carbon NMR data, and the presence of a methoxy group and aromatic protons in the proton NMR data also supports this structure. The IR spectra confirm the presence of a carbonyl group, which is consistent with an ester. Therefore, the SMILES code for the compound is 'COC(=O)C1=CC=CC=CC1'.</thought>
